source.title: Latent Adversarial Training Improves Robustness to Persistent Harmful Behaviors in LLMs
source.authors: A. Sheshadri; Aidan Ewart; Phillip Guo; Aengus Lynch; Cindy Wu; V. Hebbar; Henry Sleight; Asa Cooper Stickland; Ethan Perez; Dylan Hadfield-Menell; Stephen Casper

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests unlearning and recovery attacks, finds substantial relearning from a two-example batch, and reports that targeted LAT reduces—but does not eliminate—this vulnerability.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates unlearning with prompt variants and few-shot fine-tuning. It does not test activation-direction ablation or quantization. Layer and perturbation choices used to select training settings are not recorded as results. The Harry Potter familiarity measure is not an accuracy measure, so those rows are linked to prompting-only recovery, not to version A's accuracy criterion.
record.test_reason: The study applies existing unlearning methods (WHP, GA, RMU) to Harry Potter and WMDP and attacks them with prompt variants and a two-example relearning fine-tune. It reports how much hidden knowledge returns. It also proposes targeted LAT as a counter-method and measures its resistance to the same attacks. None of the three original sources is this study.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that state-of-the-art LLM unlearning is surprisingly brittle: retraining on two forget-set samples closes more than half the gap on average. Targeted LAT improves unlearning (Pareto-dominating WHP/WHP-C on Harry Potter except MMLU) and reduces, but does not eliminate, relearning sample efficiency. Results support but do not confirm that LAT removes the underlying circuitry.
record.recipe_differences: The study augments existing methods with targeted LAT. GA is a shaped gradient-ascent variant inspired by prior work; RMU follows the prior method; WHP is compared using a modified contrastive baseline (WHP-C), not only the original WHP recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that dataset, layer choice, and perturbation size influenced results. For Harry Potter unlearning, Spanish, jailbreak, summary, and text-context prompt conditions yield different familiarity outcomes. For WMDP, biology versus cyber and GA versus RMU yield different unlearning and relearning results.
record.problems: All experiments are on models below 10 billion parameters. WMDP relearning tests one randomly sampled batch of 2 examples, with the reported best result across checkpoints at 5, 10, and 20 steps. The Harry Potter familiarity evaluation uses an automated GPT-4 judge. Table 4 reports means ± standard error but does not state n there. The authors note that their training choices and perturbation settings are influential.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant separately reported results were omitted. General backdoor and jailbreak experiments are outside the listed unlearning recovery versions.

untested.parts: Relearning on unrelated or loosely related data. Only a 2-example forget-set batch is used, with the best checkpoint taken across 5, 10 and 20 steps. No relearning attack on the Harry Potter models.
No activation-direction ablation and no mechanistic test of blocked access versus deletion. The authors leave mechanism analysis to future work.
Prompting attacks are tested only on Harry Potter familiarity, not on WMDP accuracy. Only one other language (Spanish) and one jailbreak prompt are tried.
LAT is not tested against activation ablation, quantization, or larger relearning sets. All models are under 10B parameters.
Only GA, RMU and WHP variants on 7B models are tested.

missing.what: MMLU after Harry Potter unlearning: WHP 0.463, WHP-C 0.456, WHP-C-LAT 0.439, vs Llama2-7B-chat 0.467. This is general ability bearing on A and F.
Original-model Harry Potter familiarity per condition (basic 0.533, Spanish 0.683, jailbreak 0.463, summary 0.575, text 0.705), needed as reference for E recovery. Currently only in row notes.
Off-the-shelf Zephyr-7B-beta WMDP-Bio/Cyber scores (apparently 0.599/0.395), needed to judge degree of relearning recovery.
Whitened-perturbation/LoRA variant results: familiarity under the same prompt attacks for WHP, WHP-C, WHP-C-LAT. For example, WHP-C summary 0.130 vs basic 0.058.
Average WMDP gain of 15.7 pp from relearning across all models.

record.verdict_notes: Table 5 text is garbled. The reader's assignment of GA and GA-LAT cells is likely wrong. A parse treating 0.599/0.395 as Zephyr's original WMDP-Bio/Cyber, GA = (MMLU 0.480, AGIEval 0.302, Bio 0.374, Cyber 0.301) and GA-LAT = (0.566, 0.321, 0.269, 0.296) reproduces the stated 15.7 pp mean relearning gain and the claim that GA-LAT beats GA on all evaluations; the record's parse does neither. Verify against the PDF. The reader's C and D 'supports' labels with no rows were invalid and are dropped; these versions are untested. The reader gave F both supports and limits_scope for the same WMDP relearning condition; this is replaced by a single limits_scope. Harry Potter familiarity is a GPT-4-judged score, not accuracy, so H rows are not linked to A. The relearning attack reports the best of three checkpoints, which favours recovery.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests unlearning performance, some general-capability measures, and recovery attacks; it does not test every current unlearning method or all attack types in the claim.
Tests repeated fine-tuning on one sampled batch of 2 forget-set examples for up to 20 iterations; it does not test unrelated or loosely related examples.
No activation-direction ablation or mechanistic test distinguishing blocked access from deletion.
Tests Spanish prompts, a jailbreak, and summary/snippet context for Harry Potter; does not test every rephrasing, other languages, or general in-context recovery.
Tests LAT-augmented unlearning against few-shot fine-tuning and several Harry Potter prompt attacks; does not test resistance to activation ablation or quantization.

relationships.condition: WMDP unlearning (GA, RMU, and their LAT variants) followed by fine-tuning on one 2-example forget-set batch
relationships.reason: The simple relearning attack raises WMDP accuracy for every method. GA recovers to about original level (W17, W18), RMU recovers most of the gap (W21, W22), and LAT variants recover as well (W19, W20, W23, W24).
relationships.display_finding: A single two-example batch increased WMDP accuracy for every method, restoring GA to approximately original performance, most of RMU's lost accuracy, and knowledge in LAT variants.

relation.reason: It runs its own relearning and prompt attacks on unlearned models and reports recovery.

tranche.reason: Its own results show that a 2-example forget-set fine-tune brings back WMDP knowledge from GA and RMU (version A wrong). It also tests a counter-method. T3 would also be defensible.

source_check.notes: Table 5 is scrambled in the parse. Zephyr-7B-beta original: MMLU 0.599, AGIEval 0.395, WMDP-Bio 0.625, Cyber 0.432. These reproduce the stated 74.7%/59.9%; reading 0.599/0.395 as WMDP gives 92%/72%. GA = 0.480/0.302/0.374/0.301; GA-LAT = 0.566/0.321/0.269/0.296. Appendix G suggests Table 4's WHP row is the Eldan & Russinovich model. There is no fine-tune relearning on the HP models. Five authors are shared with Lynch et al. 2024.
